clean_body: The shape of things to come | Friend, They tell us that the Deep South is "permanently red." They tell us that change isn't possible here, that the status quo is locked in, and that we should just lower our expectations and get used to it. They couldn't be more wrong. __ What we saw happen on day one of early voting in South Carolina completely shattered that myth. When the doors opened for the very first day of early primary voting next door, the political establishment expected a quiet start. Instead, voters sent a shockwave through the entire region. Look at the official, certified numbers from just the first day of early voting. Day One Democratic Primary Ballots:45,966 Day One Republican Primary Ballots:10,340 That is a staggering 4-to-1 turnout advantage for Democrats on the very first day. This isn’t an anomaly. This is the shape of things to come. That kind of overwhelming turnout proves there is a massive, unnourished hunger for new leadership across the South. Voters are fundamentally exhausted by an extreme, neglectful status quo , and they are rushing to the ballot box to change it. Right here in Tennessee, we are fighting that exact same battle. Everyday families are being squeezed while supermajority politicians play culture war games. Jerri Green isn't just focused winning an election, she's committed to delivering real, tangible relief to Tennesseans, starting day one. Jerri has a plan for Tennessee: Lower the Cost of Living: We will eliminate the state grocery tax to give working families immediate breathing room at the checkout counter. Wipe Out Medical Debt: Nashville is sitting on hundreds of millions of unspent federal funds. We will unlock those dollars to immediately pay off a billion dollars in medical debt for families in need. Expand Healthcare & Protect Freedom: We will expand Medicaid to keep our collapsing rural hospitals open, and we will fiercely defend reproductive freedom so women feel safe talking to their doctors again. Fully Fund Public Schools: We will stop the corporate voucher schemes that drain our neighborhoods and put those tax dollars back into our public school classrooms where they belong. If South Carolina Democrats can turn out at a 4-to-1 ratio on day one of early voting, we can absolutely build that exact same momentum right here in Tennessee. But a historic breakthrough doesn’t happen by accident. It requires months of deep organizing infrastructure and the resources to fight back against the flood of special interest money backing our opponents. Jerri has the vision, the record , and the drive to bring real leadership back to Nashville. But to turn Tennessee into the next Southern breakthrough, we need to scale up our operations right now. = Let’s show them what real momentum looks like. What I wouldn't give for one more love letter from Charlie.

One more handwritten note left beside my coffee before he rushed out the door.

One more folded piece of paper on my pillow before he had an early flight.

One more moment where he intentionally set aside the noise of the world just to remind me that I was loved.

About this time last year, Charlie and I sat together on-stage at the Women's Leadership Summit (WLS), answering questions from young women about marriage, family, faith, raising children, and the kind of future they hoped to have one day.

Somewhere during that conversation, I mentioned the notes he would write to me.

They were one of the many quiet ways Charlie loved me.

I shared that he would write them whenever he had a moment while he honored the Sabbath.

_He never missed one. _

Sometimes they were only a few sentences, but they carried such a deep reverence about them. He'd hand me words that felt sacred.

I saved every single one of those letters.

Charlie knew how much those little notes meant to me, and now I treasure them in a way I never could have understood at the time.

I hold onto every word he left for me.

And looking back, I think about the young women in the room listening to us that night at the Women's Leadership Summit.

Because so many of those young women were longing for something this culture keeps trying to convince them no longer matters.

A strong family. A faithful marriage. Children raised in a home filled with purpose and love.

A life rooted in God instead of endless striving and the empty pursuit of self.

And honestly, Friend, I think that ache runs much deeper than most people realize.

I see it constantly when I meet young women across the country.

So many feel exhausted by the pressure to chase an image of success that leaves them anxious, disconnected, and lonely.

They've been told that fulfillment comes from constant achievement... endless comparison... putting themselves first.

But as I said last year, the enemy has a way of disguising bondage as empowerment.

I think that's part of why so many young women are drawn to the Women's Leadership Summit in the first place.

Because for one weekend, thousands of young women come together and realize they are not alone for wanting a different kind of life.

They meet other young women who still love God, still believe family matters, and still want meaningful lives rooted in faith and purpose.
---

Last year during our question-and-answer session at the Women's Leadership Summit, one young woman walked up to the microphone... and Charlie recognized her immediately.

Before she could even ask her question, Charlie's face lit up with a huge smile as he said, _" Hey! So... you're getting married!" _

The room burst into cheers as she smiled and nodded her head.

And then Charlie reminded everyone why he recognized her in the first place.

The year before, she had stood at the mic and asked him a simple question:

_" How do I meet a husband?" _

A year later, she came back to WLS engaged.

I smile thinking about how excited everyone in that room was for her.

I see moments like that every year at the Women's Leadership Summit. And after I leave, I always carry home a deep sense of hope about this next generation of young women.

Not because they have everything figured out.

But because so many of them are still searching for what is true, and for who God designed them to be.

Revival is not going to come through louder politicians or more influencers.

It's going to come through the living rooms of mothers who pray with their children, pray over their children, and love their husbands. And through bold actions of unshakeable devotion to Jesus Christ.

I believe the way a woman loves her family, raises her children, serves others, and walks with God leaves a mark on the world far greater than most people will ever realize.

That's why this event matters so deeply to me.

And when I think back on my own life, I know how true that is.

Before I met Charlie, I was not dreaming about marriage, motherhood, and building a family.

But when I met the right man, everything shifted. Everything changed.

And before doors open in San Antonio for the Women's Leadership Summit this June, I just want to thank you for helping make this event possible year after year.

Thank you for helping us continue pouring into these young women.

Thank you for helping carry forward a mission that changes so many lives -- including mine.

I truly cannot wait to see what God does through this next generation of young women.
---

**P.S.** Looking back now, I think some of the moments that leave the deepest mark on your life are the ones you almost don't realize are sacred while you're living them.

A love note on Saturday. A prayer before bed. A husband asking how he can better serve you.

You don't realize until much later that those small acts of love and faithfulness were quietly building something eternal inside your home.

I read all of Charlie's love letters even slower now.

Charlie and I built our marriage around the kind of covenant described in Ephesians 5 -- rooted in faith, sacrifice, service, and putting Christ at the center of our home.

Get married.
Have children.
Build a legacy.
Pass down your values.
Pursue the eternal.
Seek true joy.

That kind of life may not be what this culture celebrates anymore... but I still believe with my whole heart that it is the life so many young women are quietly searching for.

clean_body: | | | | | | | Friend, What I wouldn't give for one more love letter from Charlie. One more handwritten note left beside my coffee before he rushed out the door. One more folded piece of paper on my pillow before he had an early flight. One more moment where he intentionally set aside the noise of the world just to remind me that I was loved. About this time last year, Charlie and I sat together on-stage at the Women's Leadership Summit (WLS), answering questions from young women about marriage, family, faith, raising children, and the kind of future they hoped to have one day. Somewhere during that conversation, I mentioned the notes he would write to me. They were one of the many quiet ways Charlie loved me. I shared that he would write them whenever he had a moment while he honored the Sabbath. He never missed one. Sometimes they were only a few sentences, but they carried such a deep reverence about them. He'd hand me words that felt sacred. I saved every single one of those letters. Charlie knew how much those little notes meant to me, and now I treasure them in a way I never could have understood at the time. I hold onto every word he left for me. And looking back, I think about the young women in the room listening to us that night at the Women's Leadership Summit. Because so many of those young women were longing for something this culture keeps trying to convince them no longer matters. A strong family. A faithful marriage. Children raised in a home filled with purpose and love. A life rooted in God instead of endless striving and the empty pursuit of self. And honestly, Friend, I think that ache runs much deeper than most people realize. I see it constantly when I meet young women across the country. So many feel exhausted by the pressure to chase an image of success that leaves them anxious, disconnected, and lonely. They've been told that fulfillment comes from constant achievement... endless comparison... putting themselves first. But as I said last year, the enemy has a way of disguising bondage as empowerment. I think that's part of why so many young women are drawn to the Women's Leadership Summit in the first place. Because for one weekend, thousands of young women come together and realize they are not alone for wanting a different kind of life. They meet other young women who still love God, still believe family matters, and still want meaningful lives rooted in faith and purpose. Last year during our question-and-answer session at the Women's Leadership Summit, one young woman walked up to the microphone... and Charlie recognized her immediately. Before she could even ask her question, Charlie's face lit up with a huge smile as he said, " Hey! So... you're getting married!" The room burst into cheers as she smiled and nodded her head. And then Charlie reminded everyone why he recognized her in the first place. The year before, she had stood at the mic and asked him a simple question: " How do I meet a husband?" A year later, she came back to WLS engaged. I smile thinking about how excited everyone in that room was for her. I see moments like that every year at the Women's Leadership Summit. And after I leave, I always carry home a deep sense of hope about this next generation of young women. Not because they have everything figured out. But because so many of them are still searching for what is true, and for who God designed them to be. Revival is not going to come through louder politicians or more influencers. It's going to come through the living rooms of mothers who pray with their children, pray over their children, and love their husbands. And through bold actions of unshakeable devotion to Jesus Christ. I believe the way a woman loves her family, raises her children, serves others, and walks with God leaves a mark on the world far greater than most people will ever realize. That's why this event matters so deeply to me. And when I think back on my own life, I know how true that is. Before I met Charlie, I was not dreaming about marriage, motherhood, and building a family. But when I met the right man, everything shifted. Everything changed. | This time of year always makes me think about the future.

Kids are finishing school, graduating, heading into summer with their whole lives ahead of them. As a mom, I think about what kind of future we are building for them.

And I'll be honest, what I see in Washington right now worries me.

They cut Medicaid. They gutted food assistance. They handed out tax cuts to billionaires while families here in West Michigan pay more for groceries, energy, and health care. Gas prices are up more than 30% this year. The cost of just getting by keeps climbing.

This is not the future our kids deserve.

That's why I co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus. That's why I sent a letter to the Trump administration demanding immediate action on energy prices. That's why I show up every single day because the decisions we make right now will shape what our kids inherit.

But here's the hard truth: **I can fight a lot harder from the majority.**

Democrats need just three seats to take back the House. Michigan has five competitive races to deliver them. And the DeVos family is already bankrolling my GOP opponent to make sure we lose this district.

Our kids are watching. They deserve better than a Congress bought by billionaires.

clean_body: This is not the future our kids deserve. | = | This time of year always makes me think about the future. Kids are finishing school, graduating, heading into summer with their whole lives ahead of them. As a mom, I think about what kind of future we are building for them. And I'll be honest, what I see in Washington right now worries me. They cut Medicaid. They gutted food assistance. They handed out tax cuts to billionaires while families here in West Michigan pay more for groceries, energy, and health care. Gas prices are up more than 30% this year. The cost of just getting by keeps climbing. This is not the future our kids deserve. That's why I co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus. That's why I sent a letter to the Trump administration demanding immediate action on energy prices. That's why I show up every single day because the decisions we make right now will shape what our kids inherit. But here's the hard truth: I can fight a lot harder from the majority. Democrats need just three seats to take back the House. Michigan has five competitive races to deliver them. And the DeVos family is already bankrolling my GOP opponent to make sure we lose this district. Our kids are watching. They deserve better than a Congress bought by billionaires. = | | | = | = | = | = | = This is bigger than one race. But it starts right here in MI-03. clean_body: The 250th Anniversary Window Is Closing America's 250th is here—Son of 1776 will reach millions of young people, but only with your support right now. Hi there, This year America commemorates 250 years of independence. Families are gathering. Communities are celebrating. The cultural conversation is turning toward the American founding. And for the first time in years, there's a genuine hunger for storytelling that honors this legacy and explores what America has meant to the world. This moment only comes once. According to a 2024 Gallup survey, 71% of Americans say they plan to participate in 250th anniversary celebrations. They're actively seeking content for their children—films, books, and stories that help them understand why this moment matters and what their ancestors believed in. Son of 1776 is the animated feature that will reach millions of young Americans exactly when they're seeking to connect with their nation's story. But production won't complete itself. Every dollar donated today directly funds the animation, music, storytelling, and promotion that will help Gen Alpha understand the sacrifices that built this great nation. No other organization is stepping up to create this kind of content right now. That's why the Moving Picture Institute exists. | | ---|---|--- | | Sincerely, Joseph Corey Vice President of Philanthropic Investments The Moving Picture Institute | 375 Greenwich Street New York NY 10013

Peter,
I can't thank you enough.
I am beyond grateful for your support. It is the fuel that keeps our campaign moving.
I wake up every morning driven by a single purpose: making a real difference in your life and protecting the values we hold dear in Maine.
When I made the decision to run, I knew the attacks would be relentless. I am confident in my decision because I know I am not standing alone.
You have my back, and I have yours.
Together, we are a firewall protecting our common sense decisions. Again, thank you for standing with me. I would not be where I am today without your support.
Sincerely,
Susan Collins

**_WE ARE CASA_ JOINS FIGHT AGAINST FLOCK CAMERAS IN OUR COMMUNITIES** _We Are CASA_ released a statement calling for opposition against the use and expansion of "Flock Safety equipment" in Roanoke City. This call to action joins the effort led by Delegate Sam Rasoul to end the use and expansion of Flock technology across Roanoke City. The expansion of surveillance technology is a direct attack on the right we all have under the 4th Amendment of our Constitution. By expanding the use of Flock across Roanoke City, we are putting everyone's rights at risk.

Peter, this is Josh Shapiro, and I wanted to make sure you heard the big news: **The general election for the must-win Governor’s race in Pennsylvania has begun.**

Our campaign is built on one simple idea: That public service should be about solving problems — not chasing headlines or taking orders from Washington.

**That’s how I’ve led from Day One.**

When a section of I-95 collapsed in Philly, we didn’t waste time pointing fingers. We brought people together, got to work, and re-opened it in 12 days.

That’s the kind of leadership Pennsylvanians deserve: Leaders who show up, fix what’s broken, and keep moving forward.

**But now, Donald Trump and the far-right want to flip Pennsylvania and put that progress on the chopping block.**

Their plan is simple: Spend millions, flood the airwaves with attacks, and hope grassroots supporters like you don’t fight back in time.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Josh Turek just won the Democratic primary in Iowa - and he can win this competitive race and help deliver a Democratic majority in the Senate. Josh is a four-time Paralympian, a two-time gold medalist, and a proven fighter who won a deep-red Iowa State House seat in a district Donald Trump carried. He doesn't take a dime from corporate PACs. He’s knocked on doors, muscled his way up porch steps to talk to voters, and earned people’s trust by putting in the work. And that's exactly the kind of leader we want in Washington — one who is committed to fighting, to doing the right thing, even when it's hard. [**Now that we’re in the general election, we need to do everything we can to ensure we flip this state. Will you split a donation between Josh Turek's campaign and our movement right now?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3657?t=8&akid=2918%2E4032634%2EyK9pFO)

Democrats need to gain four seats to take back the Senate, and with a candidate like Josh running in Iowa — unapologetically fighting to make life better for working people — we have a real shot at winning here. body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/LkZV8_ZZqEK8PaX3vGWyPQ2?am=20&amtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=IESQIM+sL2lQ7Yi2qr4SZszT4h5HLODEHxKFiTkC2MdsS6eHEMNh7N3eV86PmTCbW8IxB57R3tgNZCmXBcmDGuvlihnaTQ1GSfD/gt/RZWbqIwKHOrxwUDrz3MlWQd3u [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LkZV8_ZZqEK8PaX3vGWyPQ2?am=20&amtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=IESQIM+sL2lQ7Yi2qr4SZszT4h5HLODEHxKFiTkC2MdsS6eHEMNh7N3eV86PmTCbW8IxB57R3tgNZCmXBcmDGuvlihnaTQ1GSfD/gt/RZWbqIwKHOrxwUDrz3MlWQd3u]
Hey Peter,
If we haven’t met yet, my name is Myrna Muñoz. I’m writing to say thank you and tell you how honored I am to have OLCV’s support. Because of OLCV, I am one step closer to becoming a state senator and I am so grateful for your trust in me. Your support is what got me here, Peter. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LkZV8_ZZqEK8PaX3vGWyPQ2]
My professional background is in education, but when I learned about SB 1586 and the threats to nature from data centers in my community, I knew I needed to step up. In Washington County we are so lucky to have such incredible soil, land, and clean water; we have to protect it. That’s one of the main reasons I ran for Senate District 15.
This past February, there was a bill (SB 1586) championed by my opponent that would have taken 1,700 acres of premium farmland in Washington County and allowed industrial development on it. This land was meant to be protected until 2065 under “The Grand Bargain”, yet here it was under threat. Our community has been reeling from impacts of data centers being built in the last decade, and SB 1586 would have allowed more of them. I couldn’t let that happen.
I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and represent my community. I will hold data centers and big polluters accountable. Data centers need to be good neighbors in our communities, not just take, take, take. Right now, they take our land, take our water, take our peace, and raise our energy costs... no more. It’s time data centers pay their fair share and are held accountable for their harms to nature and our communities, not just in Washington County but across Oregon.
I need a trusted partner in this work to stand by my side, and for me that’s OLCV. So far, we have accomplished a lot together by unseating an incumbent, but there is still much more to do to hold polluters and data centers accountable. That’s why OLCV needs you, Peter.
I’m humbly asking you to support OLCV once again so we can all stand together, in a strong community. Will you make a generous gift of $50 to OLCV today so we can continue this monumental work? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LkZV8_ZZqEK8PaX3vGWyPQ2]
Give now [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LkZV8_ZZqEK8PaX3vGWyPQ2?am=20&amtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=IESQIM+sL2lQ7Yi2qr4SZszT4h5HLODEHxKFiTkC2MdsS6eHEMNh7N3eV86PmTCbW8IxB57R3tgNZCmXBcmDGuvlihnaTQ1GSfD/gt/RZWbqIwKHOrxwUDrz3MlWQd3u]
I look forward to working with you to protect our environment, hold polluters accountable, and build a greener, brighter future for all Oregonians.
Thank you,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Myrna%20Munoz%20signature.png]
Myrna Muñoz
Democratic nominee for Senate District 15

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38192?t=1011&refcode=email-20260604_v&akid=10839%2E5885482%2EcpgDfW ]Our Revolution logo

Peter Willis,

As Executive Director of Our Revolution, I’m writing with urgency,
gratitude – and a challenge. We’re nearly halfway through primary season,
and I need to be direct with you: what happens this month will define the
course of progressive politics in 2026.

Our organizers are firing on all cylinders to get out the vote for a
flurry of June primaries across the country – New York, Maryland, D.C.,
Colorado, and Maine. Our Citizen Action team is lighting up phones and
knocking on doors, running a record-breaking turnout drive to get every
progressive to the polls.

Let me break down what’s at stake in these next few weeks:

In New York, we’re powering a slate of candidates ready to stand up to
billionaires and fight for the working class. Brad Lander has confronted
corporate landlords and stood up for workers’ rights at every turn. Now
he’s taking on AIPAC-backed Dan Goldman to win a seat in the House for
NY-10. Then there’s Alex Bores. Tech giants are pouring super PAC cash to
crush his campaign in NY-12 because he has the courage to regulate AI,
challenge ICE, and fight for union growth.

In Maine, we’re facing off against establishment Democrats who are openly
trying to take down Bernie’s 2016 state co-chair Matt Dunlap in the race
for Congress in ME-2. And we’re out there organizing for Troy Jackson, a
union leader who’s spent decades on the picket line, now running for
Governor to finally put working people ahead of big business.

In Colorado, Melat Kiros is up against a nearly 30-year establishment
incumbent in one of America’s most progressive congressional districts.
But it’s going to take a massive grassroots push to win. Julie Gonzales, a
lifelong organizer, is taking on another member of the Democratic
establishment in the Senate primary, running on a record of lifting up
immigrants and workers.

Maryland’s 5th District is seeing outside money from AI and crypto flood
in against Wala Blegay, a passionate champion of Medicare for All and
working families. The special interests and party insiders can outspend
Wala, but with your help, they can’t out-organize us.

And in D.C., Janeese Lewis George, a bold and fearless progressive, is
taking on the establishment for mayor and fighting back against Trump in
the nation’s capital. Our Revolution was by her side when she ran for city
council with a vision for true affordability, and won. Now, she’s pledging
public-run groceries, universal childcare – and we’re right there with
her.

That’s just June. We’re not letting up for a second because the truth is
our movement knows how to help power candidates to victory. Just this
week, we helped deliver real wins. Adam Hamawy, a U.S. Army veteran and
sharp critic of Israel’s war in Gaza, won his primary in New Jersey’s
12th. Smokejumper and union leader Sam Forstag emerged victorious in
Montana. And Rep. Analilia Mejia beat back Democratic establishment
challengers in New Jersey. That’s three new allies that could join our
progressive caucus in Congress — and more to come.

These victories weren’t flukes. Our Revolution has helped elect over 1,000
progressives since 2016, building power from the bottom up with our tried
and tested grassroots organizing machine.

Right now, we’re racing to reach 1.1 million voters in NY, 184,000 in
Colorado, 139,000 in Maryland, 72,000 in Maine, and 34,000 in DC. But as
the establishment doubles down, we’re up against a tidal wave of
billionaire cash and insider opposition.

grow our voter outreach in ALL these key races. And it’s all made possible
by you, our movement. Will you pitch in $5, $15, or whatever you can right
now to supercharge our June primary sprint?

If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | The SpaceX S-1 dropped yesterday. 277 pages. subject: 14 years of DACA, one shared fight. Will you join us?
body:
DACA turns 14 on June 15! Here’s what you can do now to protect your neighbors: | | | Hey Peter, Did you know an invitation is all it takes to bring your friends together to build change? All across the country, more and more of us are witnessing first-hand the attacks on programs meant to protect our families and our communities. We’ve watched our DACA recipient loved ones go without pay after losing their work authorization and protections due to unprecedented USCIS renewal delays. Between attempts by this administration to end birthright citizenship and strip thousands of our neighbors of TPS status, **we’ve had enough of seeing our lives being treated as disposable! 🙂↔️** [**✉️ From now until June 15, join young people around the country in bringing our communities together to write letters to Congress to call for a pathway to citizenship!**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpPipAiKICe39Rc2oZcK5vySi_PfttDFBd3lIFKlfUXxOVFORu4XVdJZVlhSvFsa69tGrLV7w3vhXAbiWWUd54sxyynZuHoDjvDds-V9L8FQg5Qyte4pJOOTOyj5koFKyBaxs6sB62dYquRE4LBxI9MpT9mijvZ2lo6faHKnaYzZg2Mv-73T2IPPrphidQAndPuf1Ax-FTrJU1cPH0Tq5xpxduNnURJM1Pinpp5YpIkNWYE6fsOn_Sa1As8rjA59ih/4r7/UhxSb15dQAmDc9r8wcHvwA/h0/h001.9vFZAV_UaOmCnPRfB7v1xjvaOy05QwPclKNt6gZmgmg) Most of us are already hanging out with our friends and loved ones this June — from NBA finals to Love Island watch parties to Pride celebrations. Between attempts by this administration to end birthright citizenship and strip thousands of our neighbors of TPS status, we’ve had enough of seeing our lives being treated as disposable! 🙂↔️ Most of us are already hanging out with our friends and loved ones this June — from NBA finals to Love Island watch parties to Pride celebrations. 📷 Earlier this year, your neighbors got together to write letters to community members in detention. What will your gathering look like? Peter, together, our power is so much stronger than any single one of us alone. Here’s what we’ve been able to achieve together already: ✍️ Over 11,000 of our neighbors have sent letters to Congress calling on them to support the Dream Act and the Dream and Promise Act — real solutions that would deliver citizenship and stability for millions. 💌 From New York to Missouri to California, more than 100 young people around the country have said yes to hosting a letter-writing gathering in their community. Will you join them? In unity, Ximena and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

Charlie knew how much those little notes meant to me, and now I treasure them in a way I never could have understood at the time.

I hold onto every word he left for me.

And looking back, I think about the young women in the room listening to us that night at the Women's Leadership Summit.

Because so many of those young women were longing for something this culture keeps trying to convince them no longer matters.

A strong family. A faithful marriage. Children raised in a home filled with purpose and love.

A life rooted in God instead of endless striving and the empty pursuit of self.

And honestly, Peter, I think that ache runs much deeper than most people realize.

I see it constantly when I meet young women across the country.

So many feel exhausted by the pressure to chase an image of success that leaves them anxious, disconnected, and lonely.

They've been told that fulfillment comes from constant achievement... endless comparison... putting themselves first.

But as I said last year, the enemy has a way of disguising bondage as empowerment.

I think that's part of why so many young women are drawn to the Women's Leadership Summit in the first place.

Because for one weekend, thousands of young women come together and realize they are not alone for wanting a different kind of life.

They meet other young women who still love God, still believe family matters, and still want meaningful lives rooted in faith and purpose.

---
Last year during our question-and-answer session at the Women's Leadership Summit, one young woman walked up to the microphone... and Charlie recognized her immediately.

Before she could even ask her question, Charlie's face lit up with a huge smile as he said, _" Hey! So... you're getting married!" _

The room burst into cheers as she smiled and nodded her head.

And then Charlie reminded everyone why he recognized her in the first place.

The year before, she had stood at the mic and asked him a simple question:

_" How do I meet a husband?" _

A year later, she came back to WLS engaged.

I smile thinking about how excited everyone in that room was for her.

I see moments like that every year at the Women's Leadership Summit. And after I leave, I always carry home a deep sense of hope about this next generation of young women.

Not because they have everything figured out.

But because so many of them are still searching for what is true, and for who God designed them to be.

Revival is not going to come through louder politicians or more influencers.

It's going to come through the living rooms of mothers who pray with their children, pray over their children, and love their husbands. And through bold actions of unshakeable devotion to Jesus Christ.

I believe the way a woman loves her family, raises her children, serves others, and walks with God leaves a mark on the world far greater than most people will ever realize.

That's why this event matters so deeply to me.

And when I think back on my own life, I know how true that is.

Before I met Charlie, I was not dreaming about marriage, motherhood, and building a family.

But when I met the right man, everything shifted. Everything changed.

And before doors open in San Antonio for the Women's Leadership Summit this June, I just want to thank you for helping make this event possible year after year.

Thank you for helping us continue pouring into these young women.

Thank you for helping carry forward a mission that changes so many lives -- including mine.

I truly cannot wait to see what God does through this next generation of young women.
---
| | | **For Charlie,**** ****Erika Kirk** CEO & ChairTurning Point USA

**P.S.** Looking back now, I think some of the moments that leave the deepest mark on your life are the ones you almost don't realize are sacred while you're living them.

A love note on Saturday. A prayer before bed. A husband asking how he can better serve you.

You don't realize until much later that those small acts of love and faithfulness were quietly building something eternal inside your home.

I read all of Charlie's love letters even slower now.

And as I read his words, the weight on my heart reminds me that we were never promised gray hair and rocking chairs -- even though we assumed it was guaranteed.

Charlie and I built our marriage around the kind of covenant described in Ephesians 5 -- rooted in faith, sacrifice, service, and putting Christ at the center of our home.

And it's another reason why Charlie cared so deeply about our nation's young people -- both men and women.

He wanted them to know there is still meaning to be found in building a beautiful life rooted in the things that actually last.

Get married.
Have children.
Build a legacy.
Pass down your values.
Pursue the eternal.
Seek true joy.

That kind of life may not be what this culture celebrates anymore... but I still believe with my whole heart that it is the life so many young women are quietly searching for.

As the Women's Leadership Summit approaches, I'm deeply grateful for people like you who help us continue to create a place where they can encounter that kind of faith, encouragement, and purpose.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

And before doors open in San Antonio for the Women's Leadership Summit this June, I just want to thank you for helping make this event possible year after year. Thank you for helping us continue pouring into these young women. Thank you for helping carry forward a mission that changes so many lives -- including mine. I truly cannot wait to see what God does through this next generation of young women. | | | For Charlie, Erika Kirk CEO & ChairTurning Point USA P.S. Looking back now, I think some of the moments that leave the deepest mark on your life are the ones you almost don't realize are sacred while you're living them. A love note on Saturday. A prayer before bed. A husband asking how he can better serve you. You don't realize until much later that those small acts of love and faithfulness were quietly building something eternal inside your home. I read all of Charlie's love letters even slower now. And as I read his words, the weight on my heart reminds me that we were never promised gray hair and rocking chairs -- even though we assumed it was guaranteed. Charlie and I built our marriage around the kind of covenant described in Ephesians 5 -- rooted in faith, sacrifice, service, and putting Christ at the center of our home. And it's another reason why Charlie cared so deeply about our nation's young people -- both men and women. He wanted them to know there is still meaning to be found in building a beautiful life rooted in the things that actually last. Get married. Have children. Build a legacy. Pass down your values. Pursue the eternal. Seek true joy. That kind of life may not be what this culture celebrates anymore... but I still believe with my whole heart that it is the life so many young women are quietly searching for. As the Women's Leadership Summit approaches, I'm deeply grateful for people like you who help us continue to create a place where they can encounter that kind of faith, encouragement, and purpose. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. And with the doors opening in a matter of days, if you'd like to help one more young woman find her calling, 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

clean_body: The men arrested included a teacher, a cruise ship worker... and even a Santa Claus | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Peter, Most people think child traffickers look evil. They don't. Sometimes they look like a teacher. Sometimes they look like a cruise ship worker smiling at families on vacation. Sometimes they even dress like Santa Claus. That is the terrifying truth America is waking up to. And sadly, the news today reminds us why this mission matters so much. Disney cruise ship staffers among 28 arrested in massive child pornography operation. Well-known Santa Claus among 19 arrested in child predator sting. High School math teacher among 89 arrested in human trafficking operation. Three different stories. Three different places. But all convey one chilling truth ties them all together: The people who prey on children are hiding in plain sight. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of Sound of Freedom and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, after hearing firsthand stories about trafficked children, my life changed forever. What I learned broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold like products. And most people had no idea this darkness existed. Thart's why I helped create the Sound of Freedom film. Not for fame. Not for Hollywood. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. Many people told us the movie would fail. Studios rejected it. Doors closed. But I could not stay silent. When innocent children are suffering, silence becomes part of the problem. Recently, while accepting the Catholic Champion Award, I shared the promise that still guides my life today: " I made a promise to God, to dedicate my life to ending child trafficking because God's children are not for sale." That promise became the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Today, we are working to protect vulnerable children through prevention, rescue support, education, awareness, and advocacy. We help strengthen struggling families before traffickers can target their children. We equip trusted partners working to rescue exploited children. We educate parents and communities about warning signs predators use to groom and manipulate children. We advocate for stronger laws to protect innocent lives. Jesus said: " Let the little children come to me... for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14) Every child is created by God with dignity. Every child deserves safety. And every one of us has a choice: Look away or stand up and protect them. That's why I am reaching out to you today. Peter, will you make your first gift to help stop the sale of God's children? predators are hiding in plain sight. But together, we can shine light into the darkness. Hi, this is Stefanie Brown James, Co-Founder and Executive Director of The Collective PAC.
I'm reaching out to you today via our Substack with a crucial message.
### **Our fight for fair representation is under attack.**
* * *
In April, the Supreme Court rolled back the clock on the Civil Rights Movement.
In their 6-3 decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , the GOP-captured Court effectively gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act -- the central safeguard against racially discriminatory redistricting and the legal architecture under which most of the Congressional Black Caucus was elected.
**What this means:**
This decision could make it harder for Black voters and other voters of color to challenge discriminatory maps... and easier for Republican lawmakers to dilute our political power.
That means fewer fair districts.
Fewer candidates of color with a real path to victory.
Fewer communities with the representation they deserve.
For decades, Black political power has been built one seat, one district, one cycle at a time -- most of it on ground first cleared by Section 2.
April's ruling threatens that ground. But the work continues, and so does our coalition.
### **We 're building Black political power in 2026.**
* * *
In 2026 alone, The Collective PAC has endorsed over 100+ Black candidates at every level of government.
We are strategically focused on creating a truly equitable democracy where our nation's local, state, and federal governments have diverse and talented elected leadership.
_A truly equitable democracy means Black people are fully represented in positions of power - and are able to create the policies necessary to move our communities forward._
But we're not waiting for someone else to step in.

We're recruiting candidates, training leaders, investing in campaigns, and building the infrastructure needed to win races up and down the ballot.
And we depend on grassroots support to elect bold, Black Democrats who will stand up to Donald Trump and give us the representation we deserve.
Every dollar donated helps fund our voter outreach, candidate support, and campaign operations needed to build Black political power.
**[If you care about our mission of organizing, mobilizing, and electing Black Democrats across the country, will you donate to The Collective PAC today?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/86a7057e-7a17-40ca-ac89-347b447f831e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
### **Black leaders we 're proud to support.**
* * *
Here at The Collective PAC, we're hard at work to recruit, train, and support a new wave of Black leaders who will fight for our rights, our future, and our democracy.
And these candidates represent exactly what this moment demands: courage, vision, and commitment to fighting for the communities that are too often ignored.
Endorsing and amplifying Black candidates at every level is our first step towards winning in November, flipping the House, and giving Black leaders a voice to fight for us.
Please, take a moment to read more about some of our endorsed candidates below:

With the Midterm elections just months away, there has never been a more urgent time to act.

Voter Action Project[https://voteractionproject.org/]
After the House passed the SAVE America Act (the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act), the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections, folks.

Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $25 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060426_1&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060426_1&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060426_1&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060426_1&amount=50]

We know the SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before the next election, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
If you missed it: This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $25 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060426_1&amount=25]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=060426_1&amount=20]

While Judicial Watch's election law team is proud to do the _heavy lifting_ to safeguard them in court, we want everyone who has supported us over the years to know there are simple things _YOU_ can _personally_ do to _protect elections_ in _YOUR community_. name: Melat Kiros
subject: The Sun Will Rise: Issue No.1
body:
The Great Moral Crime of Our Time
| |
---
| | | | _Hi Peter,

I want to be clear with you about where I stand. I also want you to know that you have power.
_ _With this weekly email series, I'll send thoughts from the campaign trail about what's going on in the world, and what we — you — can do about it right now._ —Melat Kiros
---
## **The great moral crime of our time**
When the U.S. violently escalates in the Middle East, you feel it at the gas pump within days. Then at the grocery store. Then on your utility bill. The price of nearly everything in our economy is tied in some way to fuel. It's a direct line from a foreign policy built around corporate profit to the cost of living right here in Denver.
| |
---
| While families across Denver are trying to afford rent, childcare, and groceries, ExxonMobile and Lockheed Martin keep making enormous profits. We pay twice: first with our tax dollars funding the bombs, then again when those wars destabilize the economy we live in.
---
| | Politicians in Washington have spent decades treating war as something that happens over there, separate from the rent you can't afford, the childcare you can't find, the groceries that cost more every week. It is not separate, and never was. I watched a genocide unfold in real time. I watched our tax dollars and the government fund it. It is one of the reasons I am now running to represent my neighbors, CO-1, in Congress.
---
| | U.S. support for war and genocide is wrong at every level. It has been the great moral crime of our time. In the wealthiest country in the world, we should be investing in housing, healthcare, education, clean energy, and public transit, not endless war and corporate profiteering.
---
|
---
| | The first step to ending the kind of horrific violence we've seen from October 7th, the genocide in Palestine, and the ethnic cleansing in Lebanon is to stop aiding and abetting it with our tax dollars. Our priority abroad must always be diplomacy and peacebuilding, and our priority at home must always be to meet the basic needs of every single American. That is why I'm running a people-powered and people-accountable campaign. I don't take corporate PAC money because I refuse to be beholden to the billionaires profiting from war, instability, and rising costs. In Congress, I'll fight for a government that puts human needs before corporate profits and political cowardice.
---
|
---
## **Take action: Block the Bombs**
| |
---
| One of the many organizations that has endorsed our campaign, Jewish Voice for Peace, provides us with two tools to take action:
---
[Call Congress](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/mkflxAGZy3SWsB6Fqd4UAlueE4PLiybq/click?signature=525466fdf8ddb9540877bdf2c25d5c0e2a1ad17b&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.jewishvoiceforpeace.org%2Fresource%2Fcall-your-senators-block-bombs-to-israel%2F)
[Email Congress](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/mkflxAGZy3SWsB6Fqd4UAlueE4PLiybq/click?signature=a6c23378b5a6a73d712c7b5aef2807d81301e426&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.jewishvoiceforpeace.org%2Fresource%2Ffund-people-not-bombs%2F)
| | **In Congress, I will join over 60 cosponsors demanding a halt to the supply of weapons and military support to Israel** — including Delia Ramirez, AOC, Rashida Tlaib, Ilhan Omar, and Ro Khana — as that state continues to violate U.S. and international humanitarian laws. The growth of BtB is a critical step toward the ultimate goal of blocking all military support to Israel.
---
|
---
## **What I'm reading:[ “Surveillance Price Ban Blocked By Colorado’s Lame Duck Dem”](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/mkflxAGZy3SWsB6Fqd4UAlueE4PLiybq/click?signature=91f7a48218626e492ef4b32846b15b4f2a1c9bcc&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.levernews.com%2Fsurveillance-price-ban-blocked-by-colorados-lame-duck-dem%2F)**
| |
---
| Speaking of rising prices, Colorado had the chance to pass the strongest ban on surveillance pricing yet in the country. _Surveillance pricing_ is when companies — from airlines to grocery stores — exploit your personal data, including shopping history — to charge you as much as they know they can get you to pay. In a streak of disappointing decisions (see Tina Peters’ commutation), our lame-duck Governor Jared Polis vetoed the bill.
---
| | [Read more at The Lever](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/mkflxAGZy3SWsB6Fqd4UAlueE4PLiybq/click?signature=91f7a48218626e492ef4b32846b15b4f2a1c9bcc&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.levernews.com%2Fsurveillance-price-ban-blocked-by-colorados-lame-duck-dem%2F)
---

clean_body: Not as a Congresswoman, but as a fellow MAGA patriot... | A Personal Letter from Rep. Elise Stefanik Peter, I’m not writing to you today as Congresswoman Elise Stefanik. Instead, I’m writing to you as Elise – a devoted wife, mom, and MAGA conservative who desperately wants my son to grow up in an America that’s as free and prosperous as the one I was blessed to grow up in. So, from one America First patriot to another: I’m worried... As the party of an incumbent President, history was already against the GOP going into the midterm elections. Now, poll after poll shows the Democrats LEADING in the race for the House Majority! But what’s truly terrifying are the voter enthusiasm numbers: Just 61% of Republicans are currently interested in voting in the midterm elections. Given the headwinds we’re facing, some have turned to despair and defeatism, acting like a Democrat victory is a foregone conclusion. But I’m here to tell you that couldn’t be further from the truth. Look Peter, surrender simply isn’t in my DNA – and I know it’s not in yours either. As America First patriots, we will NEVER stop fighting to save our country, no matter how daunting the odds may be. Did President Trump surrender in 2016 when the media’s polls all showed him losing in a landslide?NOPE! Did he surrender when the Democrats wrongfully impeached him TWICE?NOPE! Did he surrender after he was wrongfully arrested FOUR TIMES in 2024 by corrupt Democrat prosecutors?NOPE! But I’m here to tell you that couldn’t be further from the truth. Time and time again, President Trump and the GOP have defied the odds and delivered victories that no one thought were possible.We can do it again in November! That’s why I’m spending every minute of my remaining time in Congress doing everything in my power to ensure we successfully DEFEND the President’s House Majority... ...And right now,NOTHING is more important than the GOP’s nationwide voter verification initiative. We’ve identified your area as one of the critical districts that is currently UNDERVERIFIED for the midterm elections. Peter, you can help us fix that by completing your updated voter verification! Again, I’m not making that request as a Congresswoman, but as a fellow MAGA patriot who’s determined to defend the President’s House Majority at all costs. Thank you and God Bless, Rep. This one is personal for me: I was born and raised in a small town in Morris County. NJ-07 is my home district — and I know my parents, friends, neighbors, and hometown community deserve so much better than Rep. Kean, Jr.

That’s why I’m so excited that EMILYs List is standing with Rebecca Bennett in this race.

For me, NJ-07 isn’t just a battleground district or a set of lines drawn on a congressional map. Growing up here, I saw what makes this district so incredible: neighbors who show up for each other, families working hard to build good lives, and communities that deserve leaders who actually listen.

But I’ve also seen how hard it’s become for too many New Jerseyans to keep up with rising costs — from rent to groceries to healthcare. And Tom Kean, Jr. has failed to meet the moment.

Instead of fighting to make life better for my community, Kean, Jr. has been a rubber stamp for the MAGA agenda — voting to raise healthcare premium costs, give tax breaks to energy companies, and restrict abortion access.

To make matters worse, Kean, Jr. has been missing from Congress for months without a clear explanation, leaving NJ-07 without representation. **He has reportedly missed over 100 votes — and yet still found time to keep up with stock trading disclosures during his absence.**

**NJ-07 deserves better. That’s why I’m so excited about Rebecca Bennett.**

Rebecca is a U.S. Navy veteran, former helicopter pilot, healthcare leader, and mom of two who has spent her life putting service first. She served our country in uniform, built a career focused on expanding access to care and improving patient outcomes, and now she’s running for Congress because she believes New Jersey deserves leaders who put people over politics and solutions over division.

I’m so proud that EMILYs List is backing Rebecca in this must-win race. She has the experience, the drive, and the heart to defeat Tom Kean, Jr. — but she’ll need the full support of this grassroots community to do it.

clean_body: It’s time for all of us to rally around Rebecca Bennett! | = Hey Peter, it’s Lizzy Tarallo — digital fundraising manager and resident New Jersey enthusiast here at EMILYs List. I’m thrilled to share that EMILYs List just endorsed Rebecca Bennett in New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District to take on MAGA extremist Rep. Tom Kean, Jr. This one is personal for me: I was born and raised in a small town in Morris County. NJ-07 is my home district — and I know my parents, friends, neighbors, and hometown community deserve so much better than Rep. Kean, Jr. That’s why I’m so excited that EMILYs List is standing with Rebecca Bennett in this race. = | = For me, NJ-07 isn’t just a battleground district or a set of lines drawn on a congressional map. Growing up here, I saw what makes this district so incredible: neighbors who show up for each other, families working hard to build good lives, and communities that deserve leaders who actually listen. But I’ve also seen how hard it’s become for too many New Jerseyans to keep up with rising costs — from rent to groceries to healthcare. And Tom Kean, Jr. has failed to meet the moment. Instead of fighting to make life better for my community, Kean, Jr. has been a rubber stamp for the MAGA agenda — voting to raise healthcare premium costs, give tax breaks to energy companies, and restrict abortion access. To make matters worse, Kean, Jr. has been missing from Congress for months without a clear explanation, leaving NJ-07 without representation. He has reportedly missed over 100 votes — and yet still found time to keep up with stock trading disclosures during his absence. NJ-07 deserves better. That’s why I’m so excited about Rebecca Bennett. Rebecca is a U.S. Navy veteran, former helicopter pilot, healthcare leader, and mom of two who has spent her life putting service first. She served our country in uniform, built a career focused on expanding access to care and improving patient outcomes, and now she’s running for Congress because she believes New Jersey deserves leaders who put people over politics and solutions over division. I’m so proud that EMILYs List is backing Rebecca in this must-win race. She has the experience, the drive, and the heart to defeat Tom Kean, Jr. — but she’ll need the full support of this grassroots community to do it. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you for all that you do. name: Deb Haaland
subject: This race just entered a new chapter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
We made history this week. Together, we can do it again in November.
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260604_1_ak_partner_mw_dh_ford.GKe5TI&amount=5&refcode=em20260604-235&t=1&akid=236%2E127862%2Ewg-7Cd)
It’s Deb Haaland and **I am officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260604_1_ak_partner_mw_dh_ford.GKe5TI&amount=5&refcode=em20260604-235&t=2&akid=236%2E127862%2Ewg-7Cd)**
I’ve been thinking a lot about what this moment means — not just for me, but for our state.
Together, we have the chance to make history by electing the first Native American woman Governor in the country. But more than that, we have the chance to protect and build a New Mexico where working families can actually get ahead.
Because I know firsthand what’s at stake when leaders ignore people’s struggles. I know what it’s like to live paycheck to paycheck, to rely on food stamps and WIC, and to worry about whether your family can pay groceries and rent in the same month.
That’s why I’m so determined to fight for lower costs, build stronger schools to get kids reading earlier, expand and strengthen access to healthcare, and foster safer communities.
But this won’t be easy.
_As you read this,_ Republicans are watching to see if we have what it takes to stop them from bringing Trump’s dangerous and extremist agenda to New Mexico. They’re prepared to spend millions to flip this seat.
**We can’t let them win.**
**[Will you split a donation of $5 between Aaron Ford and my campaign today to help us start the general election strong and protect New Mexico’s future?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260604_1_ak_partner_mw_dh_ford.GKe5TI&amount=5&refcode=em20260604-235&t=3&akid=236%2E127862%2Ewg-7Cd)**

Be Fierce,
Deb

Peter,
We asked. You answered.
93% of you said Governor Polis was wrong to commute Tina Peters' sentence.
That's not a split decision. That's a verdict.
And when we asked what should come first in restoring our democracy, the majority of you said the same thing: ending gerrymandering, stopping voter roll purges, and closing the loopholes that let politicians rewrite the rules in their own favor.
That's exactly what Colorado Draws the Line is fighting for.
But of all the responses we got, one has stuck with us:
"I have not given up on our democracy." \- Carl B.
Neither have we. And we're backing it up.
In the courts. On the ground. At the ballot box. We're fighting to make sure Colorado's maps are drawn fairly, by the people, for the people. But we can't do it without you.
If you haven't given up on our democracy either, now is the time to show it.

body:
A recap of the priorities survey we sent last week →
#
Peter,
Last week, we sent a survey asking whether you approve or disapprove of Trump’s second term, along with a question about your top priorities.
**We heard back from 280 Voto Latino supporters, and every single respondent said they _disapprove_ of how Trump is handling issues that are part of our daily lives, such as the cost of living, the economy, health care, and immigration.**
And when we asked what’s weighing on you most right now, one theme came up again and again — _**the economy.**_
That tracks with what we’re reading in the headlines, the voter registration tables, and in Latino communities across the country.
If you’re ready to elect new leaders who are going to actually do something about the economic crisis we’re all facing, [**will you rush in a $3 donation today to help us register and mobilize voters from now til November?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260604-1-ak.2S8giU&amount=3&refcode=em20260604-212&t=1&akid=212%2E1366028%2EKvsdw9)
In 2024, Trump and Republicans promised lower costs, and many people hoped that relief was finally coming. Instead, working families are struggling with utility bills, medical bills, housing costs, and groceries. And nothing is being done to address this issue.
**We deserve leaders who are going to fight this affordability crisis.**
That’s why Voto Latino is organizing now, not later. We're targeting vulnerable Republicans who are greenlighting Trump's agenda and mobilizing Latino voters in the states and districts that will decide who represents us, who is going to make positive change for our communities, and show up in force and demand better.
**[If you want to help elect leaders who are going to combat the affordability crisis and power Voto Latino’s voter registration and mobilization work ahead of November, will you pitch in $3 right now?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260604-1-ak.2S8giU&amount=3&refcode=em20260604-212&t=2&akid=212%2E1366028%2EKvsdw9)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

We heard back from 280 Voto Latino supporters, and every single respondent said they disapprove of how Trump is handling issues that are part of our daily lives, such as the cost of living, the economy, health care, and immigration. And when we asked what’s weighing on you most right now, one theme came up again and again — the economy. That tracks with what we’re reading in the headlines, the voter registration tables, and in Latino communities across the country. If you’re ready to elect new leaders who are going to actually do something about the economic crisis we’re all facing, In 2024, Trump and Republicans promised lower costs, and many people hoped that relief was finally coming. Instead, working families are struggling with utility bills, medical bills, housing costs, and groceries. And nothing is being done to address this issue. We deserve leaders who are going to fight this affordability crisis. That’s why Voto Latino is organizing now, not later. We're targeting vulnerable Republicans who are greenlighting Trump's agenda and mobilizing Latino voters in the states and districts that will decide who represents us, who is going to make positive change for our communities, and show up in force and demand better. Thank you, Voto Latino
